description.narrative: In Brazil, the Consolidation of Labour Laws (CLT), approved by Decree-Law No. 5,452, of May 1, 1943, provides for the mandatory provision, by the employer, of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) [art. 166] and conditions the sale and use of PPE to approval by the Ministry of Labour and Employment (MTE) through the issuance of the Certificate of Approval (CA) [art. 167]. With the increase in demand for CA issuance in a context of reducing the number of Labour Inspectors, the new Certificate of Approval of Personal Protective Equipment (SISCAEPI), developed by the MTE, since 2022, automates the management of the process CA issuance reducing the issuance time (up to 60 days), as it will be issued instantly. SISCAEPI contributes to the effective supply of certified PPE, speeds up the CA issuance process, reduces operational costs, generates legal security and reliability for all actors involved in the manufacture/import, commercialization and use of PPE resulting in Occupational Health and Safety effective. The ILO provided assistance to the development of the system (SISCAEPI), in particular to the definition of the technical and conceptual parameters of SISCAEPI, in addition to the financial contribution for the development of the tool. The ILO also contributed technical support to define the strategy for the implementation phases and the types of PPE to be prioritised considering the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.

description.narrative:
The response to HIV-related stigma and discrimination, including in workplaces, progressed through Brazil's commitment to the Global Partnership for Action to Eliminate HIV-related Stigma and Discrimination, signed with UNAIDS and the ILO. With its adhesion, Brazil commits to act against HIV-related discrimination in multiple contexts, including in workplaces. LGBTI perspectives and needs have been incorporated in the agenda of workers' organizations through training and mentorship programs, involving 50 LGBTI individuals from multiple Brazilian states. An expanded non-discrimination approach in national professional learning institutions was implemented through the delivery of professional training for vulnerable groups. For the first time in Brazil, a budgeted program for LGBTI rights was included in the Government's Pluriannual Plan 2024-2027, including a goal to benefit 25,000 LGBTI individuals from all Brazilian regions in accessing employability and income generation. A Cooperation Agreement was signed between the Brazilian Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship and the Brazilian Ministry of Labour and Employment to implement the National Plan of Decent Work for LGBTI People, comprising over 60 actions across three priority areas to enhance LGBTI access to decent work. The signing by Brazil of the Global Partnership for Action to Eliminate All Forms of HIV-related Stigma and Discrimination was supported by active engagement of the ILO to demonstrate the importance and value of the initiative.
The trainings and mentorships for LGBTI leaders on the promotion of labour rights which fostered the inclusion of LGBTI people's demands in the agendas of workers' organizations were delivered by national trade unions with support from the ILO.
The expansion of a non-discrimination approach in the training program and strategy of national professional learning institutions was supported by technical inputs provided by the ILO in meetings held with these institutions.
Through development cooperation projects funded by Brazil and in the context of UNAIDS Unified Budget, Results and Accountability Framework (UBRAF) 2022 – 23, the ILO provided assistance in: a) developing the National Plan of Decent Work for LGBTI People to which both the Ministries of Human Rights and Citizenship and of Labour and Employment committed towards implementation; and b) including a Programme on LGBTI rights in the Government's Pluriannual Plan 2024-2027.
